item.title: Towards practical photosynthetic biohybrid systems
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01984-8

Photosynthetic biohybrid systems can convert sunlight to chemicals and fuels. This Perspective explores how to better design photosynthetic biohybrid systems to achieve practical sustainable solar-driven biomanufacturing.

item.title: Robust hydrogel ion channels for osmotic energy harvesting and environmental sensing
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01954-0

Salinity gradient blue energy offers a promising alternative to fossil fuels. Here the authors develop ultrarough, self-healing hydrogel ionic conductors that achieve an excellent power density while maintaining over 91% of their performance after damage and enable autonomous environmental sensing.
